It is implemented in Verilog and intended to be used as a learning tool for computer architecture. The design is synthesized for the Tiny Tapeout platform and can be tested with standard RISC-V programs. The documentation is brief but indicates a full processor implementation.
results.summary: This design implements a 32-bit RISC-V rv32i arithmetic logic unit that is purely combinational. It supports ADD, SUB, AND, OR, XOR, SLL, SRL, SRA, SLT, and SLTU operations using a barrel shifter and comparison logic. The design was extracted from a complete rv32imsu RISC-V SoC implemented in Synopsys tools on the sky130A PDK at the University of Central Florida. It is implemented in Verilog and can be tested by setting operand and operation inputs and reading the result outputs.

results.summary_before: This project is a PWM generator with timer and counter functionality, designed for power management applications. It uses GPIO pins for input and output, and includes a clock divider to generate the PWM signal. The design is intended for educational purposes and can be tested with a simple testbench. External hardware such as LEDs or motors can be connected to observe the PWM output.
results.summary: This project is a run-time configurable PWM generator with dynamic controls for period, duty cycle, and output polarity. It includes input safety clamps that enforce a minimum period of three clock cycles and prevent duty cycle overflow. The design outputs both the primary PWM signal and its complementary inverted signal, and disabling the module forces both outputs to zero. It can be tested using DIP switches, LEDs, or an oscilloscope on the output PMOD pins.
